altText.how: Right-click the object, open its alt text, and write a short description, or mark it as decorative.
altText.label: Object has no description
altText.why: People who can't see the screen rely on a short description to know what a picture, chart or shape shows.
contrast.how: Choose a darker font color or a lighter fill so the text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1.
contrast.label: Text is hard to see against its fill
contrast.why: Text that does not stand out from its background is hard to read for people with low vision or color blindness.
merged.how: Unmerge the cells, then center the text across the columns or wrap it instead.
merged.label: Cells are merged
merged.why: Screen readers lose count of rows and columns in merged cells, which makes the sheet hard to follow.
sheetName.how: Double-click the sheet tab and give it a name that describes its content.
sheetName.label: Sheet still has its default name
sheetName.why: A sheet name that says what the sheet holds helps people find their way without opening each one.
tableHeader.how: Select the table and switch its header row on from the Table tab.
tableHeader.label: Table has no header row
tableHeader.why: Without a header row, screen reader users can't tell what each column of a table holds.
